newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-ANDERLECHT LOSE OUT IN BELGIUM SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANDERLECHT LOSE OUT IN BELGIUM SQUAD.

text.p: Anderlecht players were conspicuously absent on Monday in Belgium's 18-man squad for Saturday's crucial World Cup qualifier against the Netherlands in Brussels.

Soccer union officials could not recall any official Belgian qualifying match without players from Anderlecht, Belgium's most prestigious club which has often provided the backbone for the national team.
They are Belgium's only survivors in European club action this season after beating Helsingborg of Sweden in the third round of the UEFA Cup last week.
Coach Wilfried Van Moer instead called up uncapped Ghent striker Nordin Jbari, who obtained dual Moroccan-Belgian nationality earlier this year.
Schalke 04 striker Marc Wilmots, who was at loggerheads with Van Moer's predecessor Paul Van Himst and quit after the 1994 World Cup finals, returns after nearly two and a half years.
Newcastle defender Philippe Albert, who had been left out for Belgium's two previous World Cup qualifiers against Turkey and San Marino, is another notable inclusion in the squad.
Belgium captain and Monaco midfielder Enzo Scifo is sidelined with a toe injury.
Goalkeepers - Filip De Wilde (Sporting Lisbon), Philippe Vande Walle (Ekeren)

Defenders - Philippe Albert (Newcastle), Geoffrey Claeys (Feyenoord), Bertrand Crasson (Napoli), Eric Deflandre (Club Brugge), Philippe Leonard (Monaco), Pascal Renier (Club Brugge) and Eric Van Meir (Lierse)
Midfielders - Lorenzo Staelens (Club Brugge), Nico Van Kerckhoven (Lierse), Gert Verheyen (Club Brugge), Frederic Pierre (Molenbeek)
Strikers - Marc Degryse (PSV), Marc Wilmots (Schalke 04), Luis Oliveira (Fiorentina), Luc Nilis (PSV), Nordin Jbari (Ghent)
